newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Howard says budget promotes lower rates.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Howard says budget promotes lower rates.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday the government's budget, announced on Tuesday, promoted lower interest rates by attacking national debt.

"I would say to the farmers in Australia that the best thing we've done for you is that we've reduced Australia's debt and that means we are consolidating the conditions for lower interest rates," Howard told Perth radio 6PR.

The budget, for the fiscal year starting July 1, projected an underlying deficit -- which excludes asset sales and the like -- of A$3.85 billion, rising to a A$1.60 billion surplus the following year.
The government took measures to cut the budget by A$352 million in 1997/98 and A$1.9 billion in the following year.
The Reserve Bank of Australia cut interest rates three times last year between July and December, each time dropping its overnight cash-rate target by 0.5 percentage points.
The current cash rate is 6.0 percent and markets anticipate a moderate chance of a tightening later in the year.
